sections.h2: What should a Mulberry, GA homeowner understand before selling?
sections.html:
Start by confirming which government answers for your parcel. Mulberry is one of Georgia's newest cities, and addresses near its edge can still fall under Gwinnett County alone. That single fact decides who issues permits, who takes code complaints and whose number a buyer's inspector will call.

The Census Bureau estimates 41,445 people live in Mulberry as of July 1, 2025, five percent above the 39,468 in its April 2020 base. Gwinnett County's fact sheet, issued while the charter was still a bill, said the new city would rank 17th in the county and first in land area. Neither figure tells you what your street sells for, so ask a local agent for sold homes within a few blocks.

sections.h2: Is my house inside the City of Mulberry?
sections.html:
The city offers an "Am I in Mulberry?" web app, and staff will confirm an address or parcel number at 770-341-9640. According to Gwinnett's planning notice, the city has handled the following inside its limits since January 1, 2025:

  • Zoning, rezonings, special use permits and variances
  • Code enforcement and zoning certifications
  • Building, development and sign permits, plus certificates of occupancy
  • Occupation tax certificates, alcohol licenses and business excise taxes

Gwinnett keeps plan review and inspections for fire, water and sewer. The same notice warns that the charter is being challenged in the Georgia Court of Appeals and in Fulton Superior Court, so its guidance may change with the rulings. Put any permit paperwork for the house in one folder before you list.

sections.h2: Which zoning and permit rules matter when selling in Mulberry?
sections.html:
Mulberry adopted its own zoning map on July 16, 2026, so a zoning label from the county days may have changed. The city's One Map web app shows the zoning layer for any parcel, and staff can read it back by address.

The city's FAQ answers the questions inspectors and buyers raise most often:

  • Permit applications are uploaded through the SagesGov portal, and a permit lapses after six months of inactivity.
  • An inspection must happen within six months of issuance, and requests are due by 4:00 PM two business days ahead.
  • Work started without a required permit risks stop work orders and fines, and illegal work may have to be removed.
  • Deck repairs need a permit when structural parts are involved or most boards are replaced.
  • The city allows one accessory dwelling unit per primary home, and the primary home must be owner occupied.
  • Hard surface in the front yard of a single-family house generally cannot exceed 35 percent.
  • Projects that disturb an acre or more, or ground within 200 feet of state waters, need an erosion and sediment control plan reviewed by the state.

A buyer who wants a rezoning faces a slower road. Staff require a pre-application meeting, review takes about two months, and the department takes just four such applications a month.

sections.h2: What do a Mulberry tax bill and its city fees include?
sections.html:
Gwinnett's tax commissioner sends the bill. The 2026 guide says Mulberry bills include local solid waste and stormwater fees, and the office's city-tax page adds that it collects special assessments for Mulberry. Stormwater is a real cost here, since the county's fact sheet said the city would take over aging pipes and a lake dam and put the pipe maintenance estimate at $16.2 million over five years. Call 770-822-8800 and have the commissioner read you every line on your parcel.

Gwinnett mails bills in late summer for a fall due date. Late balances gain 0.81 percent interest monthly, and a 5 percent penalty applies after 120 days and again every further 120 days up to 20 percent. Partial payments are welcome if the balance clears by the due date, and the office does not send bills to mortgage companies, so confirm with an escrow lender.

A homestead exemption requires that you owned and lived in the home on January 1, and the application should arrive by the appeal deadline printed on your assessment notice. That appeal window is 45 days. The state's one-time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant showed up as a credit on 2026 bills for eligible homestead owners.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax bill when a Mulberry house sells?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is on the hook for the whole year, and Gwinnett bills both the old and new owner after a sale. If the bill goes unpaid, the lien lands on the January 1 owner unless, within 90 days of the due date, the commissioner receives:

  • Acceptable proof that the buyer assumed the liability
  • A deed in the new owner's name
  • Confirmation that the deed was properly recorded

Contract wording makes the difference. The commissioner accepts "Payment of all outstanding taxes and assessments not paid at settlement and those incurred in the future are assumed by purchaser." It rejects lines that say the parties "agree to adjust the pro-rations amongst themselves." Ask your closing attorney for the accepted style and keep a copy of the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does transferring a deed cost in Georgia?
sections.html: The state levies $1 on the first $1,000 of price and 10 cents on every added $100 or fraction of it. By law the seller owes it, although contracts frequently pass it to the buyer, and the clerk of superior court will not record the deed until it is paid. Ask the Gwinnett clerk for the current recording fee list.

sections.h2: What should I fix before listing a Mulberry house?
sections.html:
Walk the property as a code officer would. Mulberry's FAQ flags grass and weeds over 12 inches, vehicles parked without a current tag, and yard trimmings left on a street or sidewalk, and it expects unpaved front-yard areas to stay covered with grass or ground cover.

Then gather records for any addition, deck, pool or fence. Pools need a permit and an approved location plan, fences need an approved application, and removing trees may need a limited land disturbance permit, so call the city first. Gaps in that file tend to surface at a buyer's inspection, and sorting them out early keeps a contract on track.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Mulberry house?
sections.html: A listing reaches the widest set of buyers but adds showings, repair requests and a commission. A private sale keeps the commission and hands pricing and contracts to you. A cash investor buys as-is on a short timeline, with a price set by repair and resale costs. Collect at least two written offers, compare who pays closing costs, and let a Georgia closing attorney prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Is Mulberry, GA a real city?
faqs.a: Yes. The Census Bureau lists Mulberry city at 41,445 residents on July 1, 2025, and Gwinnett's notice says the city has run planning, zoning and permitting inside its limits since January 1, 2025. Court cases over the charter are noted there too, so verify permit questions at 770-341-9640.

faqs.q: Do I get permits from Gwinnett County or from Mulberry?
faqs.a: Inside the city limits, permits go through Mulberry's SagesGov portal. Gwinnett still performs fire, water and sewer plan review and inspections. Use the city's address lookup when you are unsure about your parcel.

faqs.q: Will I get a tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: If you owned the house on January 1, yes. Gwinnett mails a bill to both owners, and you stay responsible unless assumption proof, the new deed and the recording are all in place within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: What deadline applies to a Gwinnett assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date at the top of the annual notice. Appeals can be made online, in person or by mail. Reach the assessors at 770-822-7200.

faqs.q: Will Mulberry charge me for trash and stormwater?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's 2026 guide says Mulberry bills include local solid waste and stormwater fees. Call the city at 770-341-9640 for the rate on your parcel.
